title: 1977: Adopt alternate symbol generator
body: Fixes #1977 Hi @IanMayo, I introduce new component `SymbolAssetIcon` which uses new library `milsymbol`, usage in `collate-assets.tsx`, line 154, this is just basic usage.

Hi @IanMayo, I think we are caching the icon by using useMemo at this ine 🤔

> Hi @IanMayo, I think we are caching the icon by using useMemo at this line 🤔

Yes, that cache's individual symbols - to speed up rendering. But, we still create lots and lots of symbols.

A cache would work like this

Currently:
- we need a symbol for [sidc, options]
- we create a symbol for [sidc, options]

Proposed:
- we need a symbol for [sidc, options]
- we ask cache for symbol for [sidc, options]
- cache looks checks in dictionary for entry with key [sidc, options]
    - if found
        - return it
    - else 
        - create symbol for [sidc, options] 
        - store it with key [sidc, options]
        - return it

There may only be, say 40 different symbols in the game (changing for sidc and color) - even though there could be several thousand assets in the game.

Note: we would probably still use the `useMemo` you provided above, to help render speed.

I may be mistaken @lebaphi  - but it looks like we create the cache in two places: support-panel and planning-channel.   I _guess_ we should only create it once.

issues.title: Adopt alternate symbol generator
issues.body:
An open-source project exists that renders NATO mapping symbols as SVG: https://github.com/spatialillusions/milsymbol

This could greatly open up the range of asset/entity symbols available to Serge game designers.

But, it's a broad change. We should only do it outside a game work-up period.

@lebaphi - I'd like us to do a trial of this alternate component, please.  There's lots of logic in how we create each icon type, and add the `adornments`, but I can provide that input once we've established if it is workable or not.

I _guess_ one way of doing this is to modify `AssetIcon` so that for some icon type, we provide a MilSymbol instead of the  existing `imageSrc`
